source.title: Flatness After All?
source.authors: N. Shoham; Liron Mor-Yosef; H. Avron

record.tranche_reason: The study compares Hessian-based complexity measures with generalization gaps using Kendall correlation, a different measurement approach from magnitude-scaled weight perturbations.
record.gate_note: The study reports correlations between Hessian-based complexity measures and generalization gaps. It does not test memorization of random labels, width scaling, architecture comparisons, optimizer or batch-size effects, dropout, or removal of memorized examples.
record.test_reason: The study tests soft-rank and other FIM spectral measures against a log-likelihood loss gap. It does not measure V7's magnitude-scaled weight-perturbation tolerance or training–test classification-error gap, nor compare that measure with norm- and margin-based measures. Its theoretical arguments also concern different flatness measures. No other listed version is tested.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is substantially accurate. The authors derive asymptotic soft-rank gap estimates under calibration and additional assumptions; for non-calibrated models, an error-to-uncertainty factor also matters. Their experiments find FIM soft rank and log determinant more predictive of loss gaps than trace or maximum eigenvalue, including with inexpensive approximations. Confident test-time mistakes can make soft rank insufficient to assess the gap.
record.recipe_differences: The study evaluates Hessian/FIM complexity measures by correlation with generalization gaps, rather than testing the source versions’ interventions or magnitude-scaled perturbation tolerance. It cites prior work but reports its own experiments on downsampled MNIST, CIFAR-10, and SVHN.
record.method_sensitivity: Gap-prediction performance varies with calibration and overfitting; soft-rank estimates become less indicative as overfitting increases. The authors also report different performance for full, KFAC, and diagonal approximations.

fits_no_version.finding: Across the experimental grid, soft rank and log determinant correlate with the loss generalization gap at τ = 0.84 and 0.82; FIM trace and maximum eigenvalue yield 0.28 and 0.08. KFAC and diagonal approximations retain positive correlations.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Training-data FIM soft rank and log determinant predict log-likelihood loss gaps better than FIM trace or maximum eigenvalue in these experiments.

fits_no_version.finding: Figure 4 reports better gap-ranking performance with better calibration and degradation with increased overfitting, particularly for soft rank.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The predictive usefulness of FIM soft rank depends on calibration and overfitting.

record.problems: The experimental correlations are reported as aggregate Kendall coefficients without uncertainty estimates. Figure 4 describes calibration and overfitting trends but gives no extractable numerical values in the text. The version’s magnitude-scaled perturbation tolerance is not measured.
record.rows_left_out: No study results bearing on the listed versions were omitted. Figure 1 and Figure 3 compare gap estimators and approximations rather than measuring a version’s named behavior; their precise plotted values are not textually reported.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and held-out performance compared with natural-label training.
Test error as width increases beyond zero training error.
Comparative image-classification test error and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD under specified tuning budgets.
Large-batch held-out performance under fixed epoch budgets and adapted recipes.
Dropout interventions and their effects on held-out error.
Magnitude-scaled perturbation tolerance, its correlation with classification-error gaps among comparably fitted convolutional networks, and its ranking against norm- and margin-based measures.
Removing highly memorized examples versus equally many random examples and retraining.

record.verdict_notes: Remove both V7 limits_scope labels: results for a different flatness construct do not qualify V7. Varying architecture and batch size in the experimental grid does not itself supply the comparisons required by V3 or V5.

versions.untested_parts: Memorization of random labels and generalization on natural labels.
Width scaling beyond the interpolation threshold.
Large-batch generalization under fixed epoch budgets.
Magnitude-scaled perturbation tolerance and the specific comparison with norm- and margin-based measures are not tested; the study evaluates soft-rank and other Hessian-based measures instead.
Removing memorized training examples and measuring the effect on test accuracy.

rows.measure: Kendall correlation for soft-rank and log-determinant measures as calibration and overfitting vary
rows.note: Text says results appear as expected: better calibration improves prediction, while overfitting degrades it, especially for soft rank; precise values are shown only in the figure.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Aggregate across tested models and experimental settings
reader_labels.reason: Soft rank correlates with the gap (R1), but the study uses soft-rank complexity rather than the version’s magnitude-scaled perturbation tolerance; trace and maximum eigenvalue correlate less strongly (R7–R8). The measurement therefore supports a qualified, related flatness claim rather than the specific measure named in V7.
